verified.exploit_entry_point: The product has two real entry points and every hidden test drives one: the MCP tool call_aws -> _execute_single_command -> call_aws_helper for request-time behaviour, and the console entry point main() for startup. Tests set the enforcement index and the operator policy the way the product does (the module state main() assigns, a policy file under the user's home) and assert on the tool result and on whether the executor, help or customization path ran.

src/aws-api-mcp-server/awslabs/aws_api_mcp_server/server.py:440-445 (main logs the load failure and keeps serving)

traps.shape: the request-time gate has a branch for a missing enforcement index that still allows execution unless read-only mode or mutation consent happens to be enabled; the same gate covers single commands, batches, help and customization dispatch
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the else branch reads as a deliberate degraded policy (deny mutations in read-only mode, otherwise ask for consent), and the repository's own tests patch the index to None and still expect the command to run
traps.realistic_because: published fix site (GHSA-29W2-FQ35-V728); the branch and the tests around it are unmodified upstream code

traps.shape: startup swallows any exception from loading the enforcement index and serves with no enforcement data for the process lifetime
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the failure is only logged as a warning, the repository test says the process should not raise, and aborting looks unfriendly for offline or air-gapped starts
traps.realistic_because: published fix site; the warning-and-continue is unmodified upstream code

traps.shape: a policy document that exists but cannot be read or parsed is swallowed and becomes an empty policy, so a command the operator denied runs; it is a second, independent producer of the same security decision
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the policy file is optional user configuration, absence is explicitly tolerated, and the repository's own test calls an unreadable or malformed file 'handled gracefully'; the advisory names only the index failure
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the published fix never touches the policy loader
